prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: Lange deutsche Komposita (language de).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Begriff" · longest unbreakable word 546px · one-line width 546px
  col 2: header "Kurzform" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 101px
  col 3: header "Erklärung" · longest unbreakable word 186px · one-line width 1091px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"Begriff column ~208px chops every compound into 3 pieces (Donauampfschifffahrtsgesells/chaft), Kurzform is fine, but Erklärung is pushed past the right edge with only a sliver of text and a truncated header visible — worst of both worlds: splits plus hidden content."},"B":{"grade":"poor","why":"Everything is crammed into 360px: compounds break into 3–4 fragments and the Erklärung at ~135px breaks single words into 5 pieces ('Gesellschaftsf/orm der/Personenschif/ffahrt'), making rows enormously tall and nearly unreadable, though all columns are technically present."},"C":{"grade":"bad","why":"Begriff takes the whole viewport, so Kurzform and Erklärung are entirely off-screen; the long compounds even overflow the cell border, so the table shows one column of context-free strings."},"D":{"grade":"poor","why":"Begriff at ~230px still breaks every compound across two or three lines, while Erklärung is squeezed to a ~30–45px sliver at the edge — the informative column becomes a vertical strip of 2–3-letter fragments."},"E":{"grade":"poor","why":"Three columns nominally fit, but Erklärung at ~75px yields 2–4 characters per line ('Gese/auf d/Beisp/Deuts'), which is illegible as prose, and Begriff still splits words arbitrarily ('sübertragungsverordnun/g')."},"F":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The most balanced of the fitting layouts: Kurzform is intact, Begriff at ~175px needs only two fragments per compound, and Erklärung at ~100px is narrow but still reads as wrapped text rather than character soup — the least damaging compromise."}},"best":["F"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"Column widths are inferred from the renders; for A, C and D I cannot tell whether the off-screen columns are genuinely scrollable and how wide Erklärung really is, which materially affects whether those horizontal-scroll designs deserve a better grade. If D's Erklärung is actually ~350px rather than a squeezed sliver, D could rival F."}
